{'translation': 'Reddit announced two upcoming changes that some long-time users may not be happy about.', 'index': 0}

{'translation': 'The company has already imposed one restriction on old Reddit, and now a second one has been revealed. In addition, RSS support will also be removed…', 'index': 1}

{'translation': 'Old Reddit', 'index': 2}

{'translation': 'Reddit overhauled its user interface significantly in 2018, which was met with strong backlash from users who were fond of the original design. In response to the feedback, the platform said the old interface (commonly known as "old Reddit") would remain available as long as users continued to use it.', 'index': 3}

{'translation': 'The first policy change was implemented in August this year, when the company required users on old Reddit to be logged in. Now the company has further announced that the old interface will only remain available to users who have accessed it within the past six months, with new users being shut out.', 'index': 4}

{'translation': 'Reddit stated that both measures are aimed at reducing AI scraping activity on the platform (although such activity seems to be perfectly fine as long as a company is willing to pay for it).', 'index': 5}

{'translation': 'RSS Feeds to Be Removed', 'index': 6}

{'translation': 'The reasoning behind discontinuing RSS feeds follows the same pattern.', 'index': 7}

{'translation': 'This change particularly impacts subreddits that rely on RSS to handle moderator workflows. Reddit said it is aware of the situation and has suggested that moderators use Devvit apps, such as Discord Relay.', 'index': 8}

{'translation': 'Users Are Not Happy', 'index': 9}

{'translation': 'A quick glance at the comments section makes it clear that many long-time users are quite unhappy with these latest developments.', 'index': 10}

{'translation': 'What do you think of these latest changes? Feel free to share in the comments section.', 'index': 11}
